findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed nine dented cans amongst the food storage inventory; Four cans of royal dragon hoisin sauce,  one can of baby corn, two hen’s tomato ketchup, one bamboo shoots can, and one pho sauce can. The PIC was made aware. The cans were removed from the inventory and stored separately to be returned. Ensure that prepackaged food items with package integrity issues are sorted out of the inventory at all times to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: An opened jug of milk was observed not date marked properly. Education was provided. The PIC told inspectors that the jug was opened two days prior (10/21/26). The PIC discarded the jug of milk while inspector was present. Ensure that food items are dated if they are going to be held for more than 24-hours within the establishment.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Multiple cardboard boxes of single service food containers and utensils including kitchenwares were observed being stored on the floor in the dry storage. Education was provided. The PIC assured inspectors that that the boxes will be removed from the floor. Ensure that the boxes are stored at least six inches above the floor to protect them from splash, dust, dirt, and other contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify allergen training certification for the certified food protection manager at the facility. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC told inspectors that that they will get the training done as soon as possible. Ensure all certified food protection managers obtain the allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.
